Sa loob ng electric motor, nagtutulak at naghihila sila kaya patuloy na umiikot ang motor para patakbuhin ang mga laruan!

Sa sulod sa electric motor, magtinulakan ug magbinira sila mao nga padayong moliyok ang motor aron padaganon ang dula!

What's the highest mountain in the Philippines?

Mount Apo in Mindanao! It rises about 2,954 meters tall, and it's a type of volcano. That's almost 3 kilometers straight up!

Mount Apo sa Mindanao! Umaabot ito sa mga 2,954 metro ang taas, at isa itong uri ng bulkan. Halos 3 kilometro pataas!
copy.bis:

What do we call it when many mountains are connected and lined up together?

They are called a mountain range!

Tinatawag itong kabundukan o mountain range!

Gitawag kini og han-ay sa kabukiran o mountain range!

Why is one side of a mountain rainy while the other is dry?

Moist air rises up a tall mountain and cools, raining on the windward side. By the time it reaches the leeward side, the air is dry — creating a rain shadow!

Bakit sa isang gilid ng bundok maulan, habang sa kabilang gilid tuyo?

Ang hanging may halumigmig ay umakyat sa mataas na bundok at lumamig, umuulan sa windward side. Pagdating sa leeward side, tuyo na ang hangin — kaya nabubuo ang rain shadow!
copy.bis:
Nganong sa usa ka kilid sa bukid moulan, samtang sa pikas kilid uga?

Ang hangin nga adunay umog mosaka sa habog nga bukid ug mobugnaw, moulan sa windward side. Pag-abot sa leeward side, uga na ang hangin — busa mabuhat ang rain shadow!

Where do our biggest rivers start their journey?

Many big rivers start in mountain ranges! Rain and melted ice flow downhill, join, and carry water to cities. That's why the area is called a watershed — a giant store of fresh water!

Saan nagsisimula ang mga malalaking ilog?

Maraming malalaking ilog ang nagmumula sa mountain range! Ang ulan at natunaw na yelo ay umaagos pababa at nagdadala ng tubig sa mga lungsod. Kaya ang lugar ay tinatawag na watershed — malaking imbakan ng tubig-tabang!
copy.bis:
Asin magsugod ang mga dagkong suba?

Daghang dagkong suba nagsugod sa mountain range! Ang ulan ug natunaw nga yelo moagas paubos ug magdala og tubig sa mga siyudad. Mao nga ang lugar tawgon nga watershed — dakong tipiganan sa tab-ang nga tubig!

Why don't Philippine mountains have snow, but other mountain ranges do?

Even though it's cold up high, our mountains aren't tall enough to reach the freezing level! In super tall ranges like the Himalayas, it's so high and cold that snow stays all year.
copy.tl:
Bakit walang niyebe sa mga bundok ng Pilipinas, pero meron sa ibang mountain range?

Kahit malamig sa taas, hindi sapat ang taas ng ating mga bundok para umabot sa freezing level! Sa napakatataas na range tulad ng Himalayas, sobrang taas at lamig kaya may niyebe buong taon.
copy.bis:
Nganong walay niyebe sa mga bukid sa Pilipinas, apan naa sa ubang mountain range?

Bisan bugnaw sa taas, dili igo kahabog ang atong mga bukid aron makaabot sa freezing level! Sa habog kaayo nga range sama sa Himalayas, habog ug bugnaw kaayo busa adunay niyebe tibuok tuig.

How do farmers grow rice on steep mountains in the Cordillera?

The Ifugao people built amazing rice terraces—giant steps carved into the mountainside! These keep the soil from sliding away and hold water on each step so the rice can grow.

Paano nagtatanim ng palay sa matarik na bundok sa Cordillera?

Gumawa ang mga Ifugao ng hagdan-hagdang palayan—mga malalaking baitang sa gilid ng bundok! Pinipigilan nito ang pagguho ng lupa at pinapanatili ang tubig sa bawat baitang para sa palay.

Lahat ba ng bundok ay nilalamigan o niniyebehan sa tuktok?

Lahat ng bundok ay lumalamig pataas, pero ang maliliit na bundok ay hindi gaanong malamig — hindi sapat ang taas! Kailangang napakataas para magkaroon ng tunay na malamig o mabaging tuktok.

Why does it get colder going UP a mountain, but warmer going DOWN underground?

Going up a mountain gets colder, but deep underground gets warmer! Earth's inside is hot, so going down into mines or caves means you're getting closer to that heat.

Bakit mas malamig kapag umaakyat sa bundok, pero mas mainit kapag pumupunta sa ilalim ng lupa?

Umaakyat sa bundok, mas malamig; pero sa ilalim ng lupa, mas mainit! Mainit ang loob ng Earth, kaya pababa sa minahan o kuweba, mas malapit ka sa init na iyon.

copy.en:
Did you know mountains take a long time to grow?

Mountains form very slowly! It usually takes millions and millions of years for them to build up.
copy.tl:
Alam mo ba na matagal tumubo ang mga bundok?

Nabubuo ang mga bundok nang napakabagal! Kadalasan, tumatagal ito ng milyon-milyong taon bago mabuo nang buo.
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga dugay motubo ang mga bukid?

Mabuo ang mga bukid og hinay kaayo! Kasagaran, molungtad kini og milyon-milyon ka tuig sa dili pa mahuman.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Philippines has many mountains and volcanoes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card names local landforms (Mount Apo, Mayon, Taal) but does not describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment. The mention of fertile soil is too brief and not developed as an influence.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mayon in Bicol and Taal in Luzon are active volcanoes that can erupt.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different types of volcanoes found around the world according to their: a. activity b. type of eruption c. location in the crust
assignedReviews.reason: The card only identifies two active volcanoes; it does not describe types of volcanoes according to activity, eruption type, or location in the crust as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the locations of major mountains, faults, volcanos, and ocean trenches using a map of the Philippine Archipelago, and interpret the features in relation to plate tectonics
assignedReviews.reason: The card names a few mountains and volcanoes but does not use a map of the Philippine Archipelago, identify faults or ocean trenches, or interpret features in relation to plate tectonics.

copy.en: The Philippines has many mountains and volcanoes! Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain. Mayon in Bicol and Taal in Luzon are active volcanoes that can erupt. They give us beautiful scenery and fertile soil!
copy.tl: Maraming bundok at bulkan ang Pilipinas! Ang Mount Apo sa Mindanao ang pinakamataas na bundok. Ang Mayon sa Bicol at Taal sa Luzon ay active volcanoes na pwedeng sumabog. Nagbibigay ito sa atin ng magandang tanawin at fertile soil!
copy.bis: Daghan og mga bundok ug bulkan ang Pilipinas! Ang Mount Apo sa Mindanao mao ang pinakataas nga bundok. Ang Mayon sa Bicol ug Taal sa Luzon mga active volcanoes nga pwedeng mosabog. Naghatag kini kanato og matahum nga talan-awon ug fertile soil!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Blowing wind and flowing water carry kinetic energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe kinetic energy as the movement of objects or particles, and potential energy as energy stored due to the position of objects or particles
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions kinetic energy in wind and water and its use to spin turbines, but it does not describe kinetic energy as the movement of objects or particles, nor does it address potential energy as energy stored due to position. It only uses the term in an application context, so it does not directly teach the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Blowing wind and flowing water carry kinetic energy, so they can spin a windmill or turbine
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to wind and water making objects move (spinning a turbine), which is related to moving objects by natural causes, but it does not explore or demonstrate different ways to make objects move; it focuses on electricity generation rather than the guided exploration of movement itself.

copy.en:
How can wind and water make electricity?

Blowing wind and flowing water carry kinetic energy, so they can spin a windmill or turbine to make electricity!
copy.tl:
Paano makakagawa ng kuryente ang hangin at tubig?

Ang umiihip na hangin at umaagos na tubig ay may kinetic energy, kaya pa-ikot nila ang windmill o turbine para gumawa ng kuryente!
copy.bis:
Unsaon paghimo og kuryente ang hangin ug tubig?

Ang naghuyop nga hangin ug nagaagay nga tubig adunay kinetic energy, busa makapatuyok kini sa windmill o turbine aron makahimo og kuryente!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many marine protected areas in the Philippines are looked after by the local communities and fishermen who live nearby.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that there is a need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that MPAs are managed by local communities, which is an example of conservation in action, but it does not teach the need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive. It provides no reasoning or recognition of the need, only a factual statement about who manages the areas.

copy.en: Many marine protected areas in the Philippines are looked after by the local communities and fishermen who live nearby.
copy.tl: Maraming marine protected area sa Pilipinas ay inaalagaan ng mga lokal na pamayanan at mangingisdang nagbabantay dito.
copy.bis: Daghang marine protected area sa Pilipinas gibantayan sa lokal nga komunidad ug mga mananagat nga nagpuyo duol niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mucus flows from your nose down your throat
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the nose and throat but does not identify the windpipe or lungs or describe how the respiratory system works. It only describes mucus draining and being swallowed, which is peripheral to the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mucus flows from your nose down your throat
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on the nose and swallowing but does not describe how any body system works, including the respiratory or digestive systems. It provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Mucus flows from your nose down your throat, and you often swallow it without even noticing.
copy.tl: Dumadaloy ang uhog mula sa ilong papunta sa lalamunan, at madalas mo itong nalulunok nang hindi namamalayan.
copy.bis: Ang sip-on modagayday gikan sa ilong paingon sa tutunlan, ug kanunay nimo kining matulon nga wala mamatikdi.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When the tide goes out, mudflats appear
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: relate the relative movements of the Earth, Moon, and Sun with the occurrence of tides
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the occurrence of tides (tide goes out) but does not relate the relative movements of the Earth, Moon, and Sun to tides. It only describes a consequence of low tide, not the cause or the celestial relationship.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: mudflats appear, uncovering all the little holes and animals hiding in the mud
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: Mudflats are a coastal landform, but the card does not identify them as a local example nor describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment. It merely states that animals are uncovered, without explaining influence.

copy.en: When the tide goes out, mudflats appear, uncovering all the little holes and animals hiding in the mud!
copy.tl: Kapag humupa ang tubig sa kati, lumalabas ang mga putikan o mudflat, kaya makikita mo ang mga butas at hayop na nasa putik!
copy.bis: Kon mohunas ang tubig, mogawas ang mga putikan o mudflat, mao nga makita nimo ang mga lungag ug mananap nga anaa sa lapok!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: PHIVOLCS makes lahar hazard zone maps
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use local information or other reliable sources to identify where the nearest active and inactive volcanoes are located and assess the risk of impacts from eruptions to their local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions PHIVOLCS lahar hazard maps and evacuation, but it does not help identify where the nearest active/inactive volcanoes are located or assess eruption risk to a local community. It only touches on a related volcanic hazard product.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: PHIVOLCS makes lahar hazard zone maps
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires interpreting PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring Alert Levels and demonstrating what to do before, during, and after an eruption. The card discusses lahar hazard zone maps and evacuation during heavy rains, not alert levels or the before/during/after response sequence.

copy.en: After a big volcanic eruption, PHIVOLCS makes lahar hazard zone maps! These show which rivers and valleys might get mudflows, so people can evacuate during heavy rains.
copy.tl: Pagkatapos ng malaking volcanic eruption, gumagawa ang PHIVOLCS ng lahar hazard zone maps! Ipinapakita nito kung aling ilog at lambak ang mapupuno ng mudflows para makaiwas sa malakas na ulan.
copy.bis: Human sa dakong volcanic eruption, naghimo ang PHIVOLCS og lahar hazard zone maps! Nagpakita kini kung asang suba ug walog ang mapuno og mudflows aron makalikay sa kusog nga ulan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: to hide and shelter when it's hot or there's danger!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a mudskipper using a burrow for shelter, but it does not identify or teach the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It only mentions shelter incidentally as a purpose for burrowing, without framing it as a basic need.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: digs a burrow in the mud with its mouth to hide and shelter when it's hot or there's danger!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a behavioral response to heat and danger, but it does not describe how the animal has changed to better suit its environment, nor does it use secondary sources. Burrowing for shelter is not presented as an evolutionary adaptation or change, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en:
Why does the mudskipper dig burrows?

The mudskipper digs a burrow in the mud with its mouth to hide and shelter when it's hot or there's danger!
copy.tl:
Bakit naghuhukay ang mudskipper ng lungga?

Naghuhukay ang mudskipper ng lungga sa putik gamit ang bibig nito para magtago kapag mainit o may panganib!
copy.bis:
Nganong nagkalot ang mudskipper og lungag?

Ang mudskipper nagkalot og lungag sa lapok gamit ang iyang baba aron motago kon init o adunay kakuyaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the mudskipper still needs a little water in its mouth to swallow its food
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water as needed for swallowing, but it does not teach the general basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter) or help identify them. It is only a specific behavioral fact about one animal.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Even though it feeds on land, the mudskipper still needs a little water in its mouth to swallow its food
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a feeding/swallowing requirement, not an evolutionary change or adaptation such as mimicry or camouflage. It does not support describing how animals have changed to better suit their environment.

copy.en: Even though it feeds on land, the mudskipper still needs a little water in its mouth to swallow its food.
copy.tl: Kahit kumakain sa lupa ang mudskipper, kailangan pa rin nito ng kaunting tubig sa bibig para malunok ang pagkain.
copy.bis: Bisan mokaon sa yuta ang mudskipper, nagkinahanglan gihapon kini og gamay nga tubig sa baba aron malamoy ang pagkaon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: their strengths add together to make a larger force
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and describe everyday situations that demonstrate: a. balanced forces such as a box resting on an inclined plane, a man standing still, or an object moving with constant velocity; b. unbalanced forces, such as freely falling fruit or an accelerating car
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that forces in the same direction add, but does not identify or describe everyday situations demonstrating balanced or unbalanced forces, nor does it mention balance/unbalance or the specific examples required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: their strengths add together to make a larger force
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that when forces are not balanced, they can cause changes in the object's speed or direction of motion
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes adding forces in the same direction, which is related to net force, but does not address the condition of unbalanced forces causing changes in speed or direction of motion. It does not directly support the competency's skill.

copy.en: When two forces push in the same direction, their strengths add together to make a larger force!
copy.tl: Kapag tumutulak ang dalawang pwersa sa parehong direksyon, nagsasama ang lakas nila para gumawa ng mas malakas na pwersa!
copy.bis: Kung ang duha ka pwersa motukmod sa samang direksyon, magdugtong ang ilang kusog aron makahimo og mas dako nga pwersa!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mumps swells the cheek too, but it comes from the saliva gland, not the tooth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses mumps and salivary glands, which is unrelated to the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems required by G4-L-1.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mumps swells the cheek too, but it comes from the saliva gland, not the tooth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: using a labeled diagram, trace how food travels through the digestive tract and explain how different digestive processes work, including mechanical processing, secretion, digestion, absorption, and elimination
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not trace food through the digestive tract or explain digestive processes; it is about mumps and salivary glands, unrelated to G8-L-1.

copy.en:
Is a swollen cheek always a toothache?

Not always! Mumps swells the cheek too, but it comes from the saliva gland, not the tooth — a different cause entirely.
copy.tl:
Sakit ba ng ngipin ang laging dahilan ng pamamagang pisngi?

Hindi laging ganoon! Ang mumps ay nagpapamaga rin ng pisngi, pero galing ito sa glandula ng laway, hindi sa ngipin — magkaiba ang sanhi.
copy.bis:
Sakit ba sa ngipon ang kanunay hinungdan sa hubag nga aping?

Dili kanunay! Ang mumps mohubag usab sa aping, apan gikan kini sa glandula sa laway, dili sa ngipon — lahi ang hinungdan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Muscles need energy from the food you eat in order to move!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a basic fact about muscles needing energy, but it does not describe how the muscular system works (e.g., contraction, structure, or coordination). It shares the topic of muscles but provides no direct instructional support for the competency's action of describing how the system works.

copy.en: Muscles need energy from the food you eat in order to move!
copy.tl: Kailangan ng mga kalamnan ang enerhiya mula sa pagkain para makagalaw!
copy.bis: Ang mga kaunoran nagkinahanglan og kusog gikan sa pagkaon aron makalihok!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: like a real muscle, a cable can only pull, never push.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card uses a muscle analogy to explain cable-driven robots, but it does not describe how the muscular system works (e.g., contraction, attachment to bones, movement). It only mentions that muscles pull, which is a superficial connection. The card's focus is on engineering/robotics, not the human body system.

copy.en: Engineers copy how muscles pull by using cables to move robot arms and prosthetic hands — like a real muscle, a cable can only pull, never push.
copy.tl: Ginagaya ng mga inhinyero ang paghila ng kalamnan sa pamamagitan ng kable para igalaw ang braso ng robot at prosthetic na kamay — at tulad ng tunay na kalamnan, humihila lang ang kable, hindi nagtutulak.
copy.bis: Gisundog sa mga inhenyero ang pagbira sa kaunoran pinaagi sa kable aron mapalihok ang bukton sa robot ug prosthetic nga kamot — ug sama sa tinuod nga kaunoran, ang kable mobira lang, dili moduso.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Concert halls are carefully designed for great acoustics
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses concert hall acoustics, reverberation, and sound distribution, but does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred in everyday situations such as a ringing bell or hearing noises.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: whether sound reaches every seat equally well
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that waves carry energy from a source to a receiver
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about sound reaching seats and reverberation, but it does not identify that waves carry energy from a source to a receiver; no mention of waves, energy, source, or receiver.

copy.en: Concert halls are carefully designed for great acoustics — the shape, materials, and dimensions decide how long reverberation lasts and whether sound reaches every seat equally well.
copy.tl: Dinisenyo nang maayos ang mga concert hall para sa magandang acoustics — ang anyo, materyales, at sukat ay nagtatakda kung gaano katagal ang reverberation at kung pantay ang tunog sa lahat ng upuan.
copy.bis: Ang mga concert hall gidisenyohan og maayo para sa maayong acoustics — ang porma, materyal, ug sukatan nagtino kung hangtod kanus-a ang reverberation ug kung pantay ang tunog sa tanang lingkoranan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: filters out more tiny particles
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate various techniques in separating mixtures, such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, and using magnets
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions filtering as a general concept but does not demonstrate any mixture separation technique (decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, using magnets). It is about mask filtration efficiency, not separating mixtures.

copy.en: An N95 mask fits more tightly on the face and filters out more tiny particles than an ordinary cloth mask.
copy.tl: Ang N95 na maskara ay mas mahigpit na dumidikit sa mukha at mas maraming naiisala kaysa sa karaniwang telang maskara.
copy.bis: Ang N95 nga maskara mas hugot ang pagkadikit sa nawong ug mas daghan ang masala kaysa ordinaryong panaptong maskara.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fingernails grow faster than toenails do.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a specific comparative fact about nail growth rate. It does not describe the general characteristic that living things grow, respond, and reproduce, nor does it provide instructional support for that competency.

copy.en: Fingernails grow faster than toenails do.
copy.tl: Ang kuko sa kamay ay mas mabilis tumubo kaysa sa kuko sa paa.
copy.bis: Ang kuko sa kamot mas paspas motubo kaysa sa kuko sa tiil.
